title: Positive component degrees characterize ampleness on a proper curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with topological dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $1$. Let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For each one-dimensional irreducible component $C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the reduced scheme $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], let $\widetilde C\to C$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization]. Then $\mathcal M$ is ample on $X$ in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] if and only if the degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] of the pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] of $\mathcal M$ to every $\widetilde C$ is positive. Zero-dimensional components impose no condition.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components; normalization is finite and birational by Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), and its degree-one pullback preserves degree by Tag 0AYZ (lemma-degree-pullback-map-proper-curves).

proof.text: The structure map of $X$ is of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $(1)$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] gives finitely many irreducible components. Give each its reduced induced closed structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each is integral, since it is reduced and irreducible, by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. These components cover $X$, and their dimensions are at most one: a chain of irreducible closed subsets of a closed subspace is such a chain in $X$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Write the one-dimensional components as $C_1,\ldots,C_t$. Every remaining component is zero-dimensional and hence a single closed point: the generic point provided by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] would otherwise specialize along a chain of length one. It is isolated because it is disjoint from all other components, a finite closed union. Denote these reduced point components by $P_1,\ldots,P_r$.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components, component enumeration; Tag 01OV and finite-type Noetherianity

proof.text: The inclusions of these reduced components into $X$ are closed immersions, hence finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. In particular each $C_i$ is an integral finite-type proper curve. Apply [lem-sc-normalization-exists] to $\nu_i:\widetilde C_i\to C_i$: it is finite and surjective, $\widetilde C_i$ is proper over $k$, and $\dim\widetilde C_i=1$. It is integral directly from [def-sc-normalization]: on a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C_i$ its ring is the integral closure of the domain $A$ in $k(C_i)$, hence a domain, and the generic points on these charts agree in the same function field. Thus the proper integral curve criterion will apply to $\widetilde C_i$ over the original field $k$, even when $k$ is imperfect.

source.place: Tags 0B5Y and 0BXR, lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic; replace component schemes by their finite normalizations

proof.text: Form $Z=(\coprod_{i=1}^t\widetilde C_i)\amalg(\coprod_{j=1}^rP_j)$ and the induced map $f:Z\to X$. Each normalized component map to $X$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]; the point-component maps are finite by Step 2. Repeated application of the binary [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] makes $f$ finite. It is surjective because its component images cover $X$ and each $\nu_i$ is surjective. Finiteness implies properness by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so $Z$ is proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. For an empty family, $X=Z=\varnothing$ and the conclusion holds directly: the affine-locus condition and positivity condition are both vacuous. Otherwise apply [lem-trf-finite-surjective-ample-reflection] to $f$ over $R=k$, which is Noetherian as noted in Step 1. It gives $\mathcal M$ ample on $X$ if and only if $f^*\mathcal M$ ample on $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y, finite-surjective cover argument, with the normalized component cover; Coherent Tag 0B5V, lemma-surjective-finite-morphism-ample

proof.text: For a finite disjoint union, the affine nonvanishing-locus definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] makes ampleness equivalent to ampleness on every summand. Indeed, in the forward direction restrict a witnessing section to a summand. Its nonvanishing locus is the inverse image of the original affine nonvanishing locus under a closed immersion; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] says that immersion is affine, so this inverse image is affine. Each summand is quasi-compact because it is closed in the quasi-compact union. Conversely, extend a witnessing section on one summand by zero on the others, using the sheaf gluing axiom on this disjoint open cover. Its nonvanishing locus is the same affine open, and a finite union of quasi-compact summands is quasi-compact. Hence this verifies both directions directly from the definition.

source.place: Tag 01PS, definition-ample, applied componentwise to a finite disjoint union

proof.text: Every $P_j$ is the spectrum of a field: choose an affine neighbourhood in its singleton space; its ring $A$ is a nonzero domain with only the prime $(0)$, so any nonunit would lie in a maximal ideal and hence be zero, and $A$ is a field. An invertible module on $P_j$ is a one-dimensional vector space by [def-sc-invertible-module]; choose a nonzero basis section. With exponent $1$ its nonvanishing locus is all of the affine scheme $P_j$. Thus this restriction is ample by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and there is no condition on point components.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y, isolated point summands, checked from the definition of ampleness

proof.text: Let $h_i:\widetilde C_i\to X$ be the composite of the normalization map and the component inclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], $h_i^*\mathcal M$ is invertible, and the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism identifies it with the restriction of $f^*\mathcal M$ to that summand. Step 2 gives that $\widetilde C_i$ is integral, proper over $k$, and one-dimensional. Applying [lem-trf-proper-integral-curve-ample-degree] gives that $h_i^*\mathcal M$ is ample exactly when $\deg_k(h_i^*\mathcal M)>0$. By [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] this is precisely the degree on the normalization specified in the item. The finite-union equivalence of Step 4, the point-summand check of Step 5, and the finite-surjective equivalence of Step 3 now prove both directions of the claimed criterion. In particular no degree pullback formula, smoothness assertion, or field extension is required.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, on each normalized component; Tag 0B5Y, conclusion

lean.statement: theorem isAmple_iff_normalizedComponentDegree_pos (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] : IsAmple X M ↔ ∀ (C : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral C] (i : C ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i → Set.range i ∈ irreducibleComponents X → topologicalKrullDim C = 1 → 0 < @Scheme.Modules.degree k _ C.normalization ⟨C.fromNormalization ≫ i ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k))⟩ ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (C.fromNormalization ≫ i)).obj M)
